entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Appellant-insurance company has preferred this appeal challenging the judgment and award dated 20.07.2013 passed by the MACT, XXIV Addl. Small Causes Judge, Bangalore, in MVC No.4187/2012.

entities.text: MACT, XXIV Addl. Small Causes Judge, Bangalore
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Learned counsel for the appellant-insurance company has submitted his arguments that the Tribunal has failed to appreciate the evidence adduced by the appellant with regard to non possession of driving licence by the driver of the auto rickshaw.

Tribunal has failed to notice that jurisdictional police after thorough investigation have filed a chare sheet under Section 3(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (for short 'MV Act') holding that the driver of the auto rickshaw did not possess valid driving licence.
The Tribunal committed an error in ignoring the evidence of the documents available on record and same amounts in miscarriage of justice.

Tribunal has committed an error in not noticing the ratio laid down by the Apex Court in the cases of NATIONAL INSURANCE COMPANY NC: 2023:KHC:21146 v. SWARN SINGH reported in 2004 ACJ Page 1 (SC), RAMBABU TIWARI v. UNITED INDIA INSURANCE COMPANY LTD., reported in 2008 ACJ 2654, NATIONAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED v. VIDYADHARA MEHARIWALA reported in 2008 ACJ 2860 and MALLA PRAKASH RAO v. MALLAJANAKI reported in 2004 (3) SCC 343 wherein the Apex Court clearly held that if the driver did not possess valid and effective driving licence, the insurer is not liable to pay the compensation.

sentences.text: On all these grounds sought for allowing this appeal.
3. As against this, learned counsel for the respondents-claimants has submitted his arguments that the Tribunal has properly appreciated the evidence in accordance with law and facts.
That there are no grounds to interfere with the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal.
Further it is submitted that the respondents have preferred an appeal in MFA NC: 2023:KHC:21146 No.10636/2013 for enhancement of compensation, which was dismissed by this Court on 17.12.2015.

4. Having heard the arguments on both sides, the following points would arise for my consideration:
(1) Whether the appellant-insurance company has made out grounds to interfere with the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal as to the liability of the insurance company?
(2) What order/award?

5. My answer to the above points are as follows:
(1) Negative (2) As per final order 5.
I have gone through the impugned judgment and award.
A perusal of impugned judgment it is clear that the insurance company has taken defence that the driver of the goods auto was not having valid licence at the time of accident.

6. The Tribunal has observed that in Ex.P-2 - charge sheet it has observed that police have not inserted offences punishable under Section 3(1) r/w 181 of MV Act, but in Ex.R-2 it is shown that the accused has committed an offence punishable under Section 279 and 304-A of IPC and Section 181 of MV Act.

The IO examined before the Court as RW2 has deposed in his evidence that he is the IO in this crime number, but he has denied that Ex.P-4 - charge sheet does not reveal as to the offence punishable under Section 3(1) r/w 181 of MV Act.
In Ex.P-4 he has not explained even during his examination before the Court on oath as to why he has not inserted Section 3(1) r/w 181 of the MV Act.
Ex.P-4 is contrary to the contents of Ex.R-2 as to the alleged commission of offence punishable under Section 3(1) r/w 181 of the MV Act.

The IO who is examined before the Court has not deposed in his evidence during the course of investigation, whether he has issued notice to the owner of the vehicle as required under Section 133 of the MV Act or not.

Considering all these aspects and also relying on the NC: 2023:KHC:21146 judgments of Hon'ble Apex Court and this Court, the Tribunal has held that insurance company has not discharged the burden to prove that the driver was not having valid driving licence at the time of accident.

He has relied on the judgment of Supreme Court in the case of 1999 ACJ 171 (RUKMANI & ORS. v. NEW INDIA ASSURANCE CO. LTD.), ILR 2000 KAR 2829 (UNITED INDIA INSURANCE CO. LTD. v. N.SRINIVASA & ANOTHER), 2004 ACJ 677 (ORIENTAL INSURANCE COMPANY LTD., v. RAMESH B. JAIN AND OTHERS), 2005 ACJ 89 (RANGAPPA & ORS. v. B.L.MAHALINGAPPA & ORS.), and 2005 ACJ 92 (SANDHYA DEBEY &
ORS. v. SHYAM KUMAR & ORS.).

sentences.text: 7. On re-appreciation of evidence on record also, I do not find any legal infirmities in the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal.
The Tribunal has awarded the compensation in accordance with law and facts.

Accordingly, that there are no grounds to interfere NC:
2023:KHC:21146 with the impugned judgment and award as to the insurance company.

RE. POINT NO.2:
8.

For the aforestated reasons and discussion, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER (1) Appeal is dismissed.
(2) Amount in deposit, if any, shall be transmitted to the jurisdictional Court to disburse the same to the claimants in terms of the award of the Tribunal.
(3) Registry is directed to transmit the records to the jurisdictional court along with the copy of this judgment.
